mechanism_narrative: A negative month-over-month change in the federal funds rate compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future S&P 500 cash flows and generating positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days as observed in historical monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: In the 20-day forward returns following any negative month-over-month change in FEDFUNDS, the average return is negative or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 7.5% signals persistent labor market weakness, which is associated with reduced consumer confidence and corporate profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 5-day forward returns following any month with UNRATE > 7.5%, the average return is positive or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in GDP (GDPC1 above 1-year moving average) and consumer spending (RSAFS above 1-year moving average) signals a robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 60-day forward returns following any instance where both GDPC1 and RSAFS are above their 1-year moving averages, the average return is negative or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening supply capacity, which may lead to higher inflation and aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day forward returns following any month-over-month decline in INDPRO during late-cycle expansions, the average return is positive or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, which may lead to premature monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day forward returns following any month with CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, the average return is positive or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals strengthening labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 5-day forward returns following any positive month-over-month change in PAYEMS, the average return is negative or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST above 1-month moving average) and consumer spending (RSAFS above 1-month moving average) signals a broad-based economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 60-day forward returns following any instance where both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 1-month moving averages, the average return is negative or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a month-over-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a shift to restrictive policy, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day forward returns following any month-over-month increase in FEDFUNDS during monetary tightening cycles, the average return is positive or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
